comparator.name: Natural Sciences
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 formally adopted Faculty of Science EER; current 180-EC standard route
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 EER, Arts. 7.3–7.5, defines 60 EC first-year compulsory physics, mathematics, chemistry and biochemistry; 30 EC later shared compulsory courses; a 72-EC formal specialisation; 6 EC free electives; and a 12-EC Bachelor’s Internship and Report as individual final project. For the first-listed Physical Chemistry specialisation, 33 EC of named courses are required and 39 EC is restricted choice from eligible non-overlapping Faculty of Science bachelor courses and/or a permitted minor. Total: 60+30+33+39+6+12=180. The other two specialisations, Biophysics and Biochemistry, are mutually exclusive and are not mixed into this route. First-listed instances are used only for alternative course groups within the selected route; they are not UCR-matching selections. The 0-EC first-year Academic Skills subcomponent and RADAr assessment carry no additional credits. Prospective 2027–28 programme pages illustrate routes but the adopted 2026–27 EER controls requirements. The programme language is Dutch though most courses are taught in English.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target names no specialisation. The adopted EER offers three equally formal combinations of two natural sciences, each with a common 60-EC first year and 30-EC later core; it identifies no general unspecialised route. The first-listed Physical Chemistry option is the neutral official-order tie break after testing for a broader route, without reference to the UCR catalogue.

exception.reason: Radboud Natural Sciences teaches physics, chemistry, (molecular) biology and mathematics together. The compulsory first year includes chemical analysis and lab, organic chemistry and synthesis lab, atoms and molecules, biochemistry, thermodynamics, mechanics and lab, and electromagnetism; the shared later core adds quantum mechanics and vector calculus. The selected physical-chemistry route requires advanced mechanics, electromagnetism, spectroscopy, chemical bonding and physical organic chemistry. UCR has viable biology, environmental science, data and mathematics courses, but it has no taught sequence in chemistry or core mechanics/electromagnetism/quantum physics. Its few relevant biochemistry and broad life-science lab offerings cannot stand in for the missing experimental chemistry and physics. A 24-course environmental/biomedical/data curriculum would be a different degree, not a faithful closest response to this exact target.
exception.curriculumContext: The adopted 2026–27 EER establishes a coherent 180-EC first-listed Physical Chemistry route; the 39-EC restricted specialisation choice and 6-EC open free space are kept separate. All three specialisations share a mandatory physics/chemistry core, so selecting Biophysics or Biochemistry would not fix the substantive UCR gap.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Read all 151 rows of data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx on the current GitHub main version, including descriptions, outline-based profiles, disciplines, prerequisites and 2026–29 availability. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory address biology and a limited molecular lab; DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus and DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming address some mathematical and computational techniques. ENSSUST111 Climate Change, ENSENVI111 Dynamic Earth and ENSENVI213 Earth System Science Tools address environmental systems. No UCR courses supply first-year organic chemistry, chemical analysis and synthesis labs, mechanics and electromagnetism, nor a progressive quantum/physical-chemistry and advanced physics route. An academically coherent 24-course arrangement could draw on the cited areas but would omit the external degree’s defining mandatory laboratory and disciplinary spine.
